servodutil: add SIGKILL for thorny servod instances This change does two things (1) waits until the process is no longer alive before returning after sending stop, so the user has some guarantee that the turn down process has finished (2) sends a SIGKILL to servod if after a given timeout (5s now) the servod instance has still not turned donw. BUG=chromium:917767 TEST=manual testing (1) normal flow - start servod $ sudo servodutil stop -p 9999 SIGTERM sent to servod instance associated with id '9999'. 2019-07-15 07:54:30,093 - servod - INFO - Received signal: 15. Attempting to turn off [...] Servod instance associated with id '9999' turned down. (2) Sigkill flow - comment out SIGTERM line - start servod $ sudo servodutil stop -p 9999 SIGTERM sent to servod instance associated with id '9999'. Servod instance associated with '9999' (pid '94388') did not turn down after SIGTERM. Sending SIGKILL. [1]+ Killed sudo servod -b atlas -s 54 Change-Id: I6f3eb9b6c2f81536afbca5646f2a0ae834c9c72c Signed-off-by: Ruben Rodriguez Buchillon <coconutruben@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1700794 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Wai-Hong Tam <waihong@google.com>
